actions.name: ButtonVerify_Click
actions.purpose: Parses the SPOL text and reports whether it is valid and how many policy settings it holds.

context.scope: Action started by a person in the ImportSpol screen of Setting policies: Parses the SPOL text and reports whether it is valid and how many policy settings it holds.
rules: A policy-state script (SPOL) that fails to load is reported with the parser's message plus '(Error found on line N.)'. (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:6)

Verify reads the text as an SPOL file: valid text reports "Validation successful, N policy settings found."; invalid text reports "SPOL validation failed: " and the reason. Nothing is applied. (PolicyPlus/ImportSpol.vb:12)
A SPOL script is refused unless its first line is 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy', with the message 'Incorrect signature.' (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:50)
In a SPOL script a policy header starting with 'U' is a user-section policy; any other first letter is treated as computer section. The rest is the policy ID. (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:53)

A SPOL script is refused, with the line number, when a policy header has no space between section and policy ID, or when the header is last in the text, or the state line is missing after it. (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:53)

In a SPOL script an optional 'Comment:' line follows the header; '\\' stands for a backslash and '\n' for a line break. A backslash at the end of the comment, or followed by any other character, is refused ('Escape sequence started at end of comment.' / 'Unknown comment escape sequence'). (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:56)
A SPOL policy state must be 'Not Configured', 'Enabled' or 'Disabled' (any case); anything else is refused with 'Unknown policy state.' (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:78)
Option lines in a SPOL script are read only for Enabled policies, until a blank line. (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:88)
unconfirmed: For the capability: Whether a policy save asks Windows to refresh or the program applies the change itself depends on a fixed list of Windows edition codes. Whether newer editions are on that list is assumed. If wrong: On an unlisted edition with Group Policy, saves would apply changes to the registry directly instead of refreshing policy.

For the capability: Which Windows edition the computer is, and so whether Group Policy tools are offered, comes from a Windows system call. The code holds only a list of accepted edition codes, so new editions are missed until it is updated. If wrong: A supported edition is wrongly reported as lacking Group Policy, or an unsupported one passes.

actions.purpose: Fills the dialog from the chosen policy when it opens

context.scope: Action started by another system in the EditSetting screen of Setting policies: Fills the dialog from the chosen policy when it opens
rules: For a checkbox element queued for deletion counts as one disabled element. (PolicyPlus/PolicyProcessing.vb:11)
The 'supported on' box shows the supported platform name, or is empty when the policy declares none. (PolicyPlus/EditSetting.vb:20)

A policy with a registry value counts toward Enabled when that value holds its on value (or the number 1 when none is defined), and toward Disabled when it holds its off value (or is queued for deletion when none is defined). (PolicyPlus/PolicyProcessing.vb:20)
Registry keys and value names in a policy file are matched ignoring case; the first spelling met is kept and written back out. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:20)

actions.purpose: Applies the chosen state to the policy source and closes

context.scope: Action started by a person in the EditSetting screen of Setting policies: Applies the chosen state to the policy source and closes
rules: Deleting a value in a POL file first forgets any value and marker for it. Unless it is already queued, a '**del.<name>' marker with the number 32 is then added, as Microsoft does. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:92)
Forgetting a value in a POL file removes both its value record and its deletion marker, so it returns to Not configured. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:99)

Setting a value in a POL file replaces any earlier record of the same value with the new data and kind. An existing deletion marker is not removed; the value record wins when the file is read. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:105)
Clearing a key in a POL file forgets every value and marker in the key, and adds a '**delvals.' marker, so the key is in the state Key cleared. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:183)

Each listed user hive is marked Yes when it can be opened for reading and writing and the program runs as an administrator, No (unprivileged) when it opens but the program is not an administrator, No when access is denied, and No (in use) for any other failure to open it. (PolicyPlus/OpenUserRegistry.vb:8)

The user hive list shows each folder under C:\Users that holds an ntuser.dat file, skipping folders that are links (reparse points). Folders without an ntuser.dat are not listed. (PolicyPlus/OpenUserRegistry.vb:9)

Verify reads the text as an SPOL file: valid text reports "Validation successful, N policy settings found."; invalid text reports "SPOL validation failed: " and the reason. Nothing is applied. (PolicyPlus/ImportSpol.vb:12)

Pressing the Cancel button (also labelled Close, and the dialog's cancel button) closes the setting dialog reporting OK if at least one Apply was done during this opening, and Cancel otherwise. The OK button always reports OK. (PolicyPlus/EditSetting.vb:15)
When the per-user policy dialog is confirmed with a user name but no SID, the name is searched first; if that finds no SID the dialog stays open. (PolicyPlus/OpenUserGpo.vb:15)
unconfirmed: For the capability: Whether a policy save asks Windows to refresh or the program applies the change itself depends on a fixed list of Windows edition codes. For the capability: Which Windows edition the computer is, and so whether Group Policy tools are offered, comes from a Windows system call. The code holds only a list of accepted edition codes, so new editions are missed until it is updated. If wrong: A supported edition is wrongly reported as lacking Group Policy, or an unsupported one passes.

rules: In the policy sources dialog the computer registry text box is enabled only for the registry choice; the computer POL file name box and Browse button only for the POL file choice. (PolicyPlus/OpenPol.vb:46)

In the policy sources dialog the user registry box is enabled only for the registry choice, the POL file box and Browse only for the file choice, the SID box and Browse only for the per-user policy choice, and the hive path box and Browse only for the per-user hive choice. (PolicyPlus/OpenPol.vb:54)

Choosing a POL file in the policy sources dialog offers only .pol files and does not warn when the chosen file already exists, so an existing or new file name can be picked. (PolicyPlus/OpenPol.vb:38)

A registry policy source accepts the root key names hkcu, hkey_current_user, hku, hkey_users, hklm and hkey_local_machine in any letter case; any other root is refused with "The root key is not valid." A path after the root is created if missing. (PolicyPlus/PolicyLoader.vb:21)

When the policy sources dialog is accepted, the computer source is the local policy, the typed registry path, the typed POL file, or an empty scratch space, as chosen. If it cannot be created, the dialog stays open and the person is told "The computer policy loader could not be created. " followed by the reason. (PolicyPlus/OpenPol.vb:79)

The local policy source uses the Machine or User Registry.pol under the Windows GroupPolicy folder and its gpt.ini; a per-user policy source uses GroupPolicyUsers\<SID>\User\Registry.pol and that folder's gpt.ini. (PolicyPlus/PolicyLoader.vb:17)

Checks the SID is valid and closes the dialog with it as the answer.
Empties the user name and SID boxes when the dialog appears.
Closes the dialog as cancelled when Escape is released.
rules: When a user name is searched in the per-user policy dialog, it is translated to a SID shown in the SID box; if Windows cannot translate it the person is told "The name could not be translated to a SID." (PolicyPlus/OpenUserGpo.vb:7)

When the per-user policy dialog is confirmed with a SID that is not a valid SID, it stays open and the person is told "The SID is not valid. Enter a SID in the lower box, or enter a username in the top box and press Search to translate."; a valid SID is returned. (PolicyPlus/OpenUserGpo.vb:20)
When the per-user policy dialog is confirmed with a user name but no SID, the name is searched first; if that finds no SID the dialog stays open. (PolicyPlus/OpenUserGpo.vb:15)
The per-user policy dialog clears both the user name and SID boxes each time it opens. (PolicyPlus/OpenUserGpo.vb:31)
unconfirmed: For the capability: Whether a policy save asks Windows to refresh or the program applies the change itself depends on a fixed list of Windows edition codes. Whether newer editions are on that list is assumed. If wrong: On an unlisted edition with Group Policy, saves would apply changes to the registry directly instead of refreshing policy.

For the capability: Which Windows edition the computer is, and so whether Group Policy tools are offered, comes from a Windows system call. The code holds only a list of accepted edition codes, so new editions are missed until it is updated. If wrong: A supported edition is wrongly reported as lacking Group Policy, or an unsupported one passes.

concerns.name: Reading and writing policy values in policy files and the registry
concerns.purpose: Every policy lookup and change goes through one store of keys and values, held in a policy file or the live registry. Browsing, setting, raw editing and loading all lean on it, as does definition management.

concerns.name: Looking up display text from definition strings
concerns.purpose: Policy names and descriptions are written as string codes in the definition files. This turns a code into text for the language loaded, and every screen showing policy text relies on it.

concerns.name: Enabling Windows privileges for protected files and hives
concerns.purpose: Before loading user policy hives or replacing protected definition files, the program asks Windows for backup, restore or ownership rights. Loading policy sources, policy setting and definition download lean on it.

concerns.name: Checking whether this Windows edition has Group Policy
concerns.purpose: Tells the program whether the machine's Windows edition includes the Group Policy machinery, so it can adapt what it offers. Start-up and policy source loading use it.

openPoints.statement: Whether a policy save asks Windows to refresh or the program applies the change itself depends on a fixed list of Windows edition codes. Whether newer editions are on that list is assumed.
openPoints.why: The list is a fixed set of numbers; which Windows editions they stand for is outside the code.
openPoints.ifWrong: On an unlisted edition with Group Policy, saves would apply changes to the registry directly instead of refreshing policy.

openPoints.statement: Which Windows edition the computer is, and so whether Group Policy tools are offered, comes from a Windows system call. The code holds only a list of accepted edition codes, so new editions are missed until it is updated.
openPoints.why: The edition code is returned by the operating system; the list's coverage of current Windows editions is not checkable from the code.
openPoints.ifWrong: A supported edition is wrongly reported as lacking Group Policy, or an unsupported one passes.
